top.title: Inter star Francesco Pio Esposito sets incredible record as Italy’s most efficient goalscorer in history
top.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-ITA-FRA - AFP Inter sensation Francesco Pio Esposito has made Italian football history by recording the best goals-per-minute ratio ever seen for the national team. The young striker has surprisingly surpassed Azzurri legends like Luigi Riva and Silvio Piola with his prolific international strike rate. Setting a new Italian scoring record Esposito has officially written his name into the Italian football history books. The 21-year-old has established the best goals-per-minute ratio ever recorded for the Italy national team. The Inter striker has been in sensational form on the international stage, netting nine goals in just 14 appearances for his country. That includes his two goals during the Azzurri’s 3-1 comeback victory over France at the San Siro. That remarkable return equates to a phenomenal average of one goal every 88 minutes. This astonishing strike rate places the young forward at the very top of Italy's all-time efficiency charts. He has now comfortably outpaced several renowned figures who previously dominated the international scoring rankings. Surpassing former forward Enrico Chiesa To put Esposito's remarkable achievement into perspective, his ruthless finishing has seen him eclipse Enrico Chiesa in the record books. Chiesa previously held a highly respected benchmark, averaging a goal every 91 minutes. However, Chiesa only managed to score seven times during his entire international career with the Azzurri. Esposito has already bypassed that overall tally while maintaining a superior scoring frequency. The third-ranked player on this exclusive list is Julio Libonatti, a striker with dual Argentine-Italian citizenship. Libonatti, who represented Italy between 1926 and 1932, scored 15 goals in 17 games at a rate of one every 102 minutes. Bettering true Italian football legends Perhaps the most impressive aspect of Esposito's record is that he is currently outperforming Italy's greatest ever strikers. Luigi Riva, the all-time leading scorer in the history of the national side, sits further down the efficiency list. Riva famously netted 35 times for the Azzurri, a total unmatched by any other Italian player. Yet, his legendary strike rate stood at one goal every 106 minutes, firmly behind Esposito's current pace. Meanwhile, Silvio Piola, who ranks third on Italy's all-time top scorers list with 30 goals, averaged a strike every 103 minutes. What's next for Esposito? As a player with immense potential, Esposito will now focus on maintaining this historic momentum. Sustaining a goal every 88 minutes over a long career will be a monumental challenge, but the early signs are hugely promising. The 21-year-old must now translate this ruthless international form into consistent club performances to secure a regular starting berth. top.title: Jürgen Klopp praises Brajan Gruda after stunning goal on Germany debut
top.description: Jürgen Klopp praises Brajan Gruda after stunning goal on Germany debut An assist against Manchester City, two against FC Augsburg and now a goal on his debut for the Germany senior national team . Brajan Gruda was named in the starting XI for Germany’s 3-1 win over Serbia in the Nations League, wearing the number ten shirt. Head coach Jürgen Klopp had already described the Leipzig attacker as a “street footballer, simply a brilliant player to watch” ahead of the match. Gruda with a solo run from his own half Operating on the right wing, Brajan repeatedly looked to take on his man against a Serbia side sitting deep. After around 20 minutes, he delivered a pinpoint cross onto the head of Kai Havertz. Shortly after the break, Gruda embarked on a solo run during a spell of Serbian pressure. Receiving a low pass from Joshua Kimmich, he turned away from his marker inside his own half . Approaching the penalty area, he left another defender trailing before slotting a low left-footed finish into the bottom-right corner . Nine successful dribbles on Germany debut - only Jamal Musiala has managed more Against Serbia, Brajan completed nine of his 14 attempted dribbles . According to Opta, only Jamal Musiala has recorded more successful dribbles in a single appearance for Germany over the past ten years. Musiala managed 13 against Costa Rica at the 2022 World Cup. “ It was instinct. I don’t think too much when I’m dribbling with the ball. I just do it . It just happens,” Brajan said of his goal. Klopp summed up the moment in his interview with RTL: “Brajan then calmly put an end to the opposition’s brief resurgence.” Klopp raves about Gruda’s feel for the game “What a debut,” said RTL commentator Wolff-Christoph Fuss as Brajan was substituted off in the 86th minute. Klopp was particularly impressed by the way Gruda switched between keeping things simple and taking on opponents with daring dribbles. “Brajan is an exceptional talent ; he has exceptional ability . The way he mixed things up today, playing simple passes before taking risks again – it was really lovely to watch .” Germany face the Netherlands on Monday evening. Asked whether he could feature in the starting XI again, Brajan replied: “Thankfully, I’ve come through it well. top.title: Triumphant Democrats descend on COP31 snubbed by Trump
top.description: Fresh from their US midterm election triumph, an emboldened group of Democratic lawmakers descended on the COP31 climate talks shunned by President Donald Trump on Saturday to signal their commitment to tackling global warming. The 18-strong delegation joined the annual UN conference in Turkey after their party regained control of both chambers of Congress in a landslide victory last week cheered by climate campaigners. “Many of our allies and partners across the world think the United States has not been predictable or dependable. So we have a lot of trust to earn back,” Florida Representative Kathy Castor told AFP. “We have so much work to do. And yes, I hope the United States gets back on track with urgent climate action,” she said after the group took photos in front of a large COP31 sign in a sprawling expo centre. The election has been a topic of discussion at COP31 in Antalya, with hopes that Democrats can restore some clean energy policies and that a pro-climate president can be elected in two years. “What happened in the US is remarkable, and a much needed shift that we all needed, not only from a climate perspective, but overall,” Harjeet Singh, strategic advisor to the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative, told AFP. Since taking office in January 2025, Trump has rolled back some of the clean energy policies of his predecessors, promoted oil drilling, pulled the United States out of the Paris Agreement and kept his country out of the UN’s climate negotiations. “It is absolutely shameful that the Trump administration operates this way, that this is an administration that is filled with climate deniers, that is beholden to big oil in the United States,” Yassamin Ansari, an Arizona lawmaker, told AFP. – ‘Climate action alive in America’ – Ansari and other members of the delegation spoke at a panel focused on the midterm elections, attracting a crowd that overflowed outside the “America Is All In” pavilion. The group reminded COP31 delegates that, while Trump has rejected clean energy, US states and local governments have continued to promote renewables and other pro-climate policies. A group of US mayors and governors visited COP31 earlier this week, along with former US vice president Al Gore and former US climate envoy and secretary of state John Kerry. “Despite the setbacks that we’re experiencing through this Trump administration, climate action is alive in America,” California Congressman Raul Ruiz told the panel. The president’s Republican party was handed a resounding defeat last week in large part due to anger over soaring energy prices and Trump’s costly war with Iran. Democrats have vowed to use their majority in the House and the Senate to launch investigations into the administration’s climate policies and propose clean energy legislation. top.title: Kimi Antonelli meets Italian president Sergio Mattarella
top.description: Motorsport photo "To President Mattarella, with great admiration," signed Kimi Antonelli . The new Formula 1 world champion is in the middle of a whirlwind of meetings, events and celebrations for the world title he won two weeks ago at the Mexico Grand Prix, with which he ended a title drought for an Italian driver to win the world championship dating back to 1953. Antonelli, together with his parents Marco and Veronica and his sister Maggie, was received on Friday by the president of the Italian Republic, Sergio Mattarella. The meeting took place at the Quirinale in Rome, with Antonelli giving the president one of his official helmets with a dedication written on the visor. Il Presidente Sergio Mattarella con Kimi Antonelli, Campione del mondo di Formula 1 Il Presidente Sergio Mattarella con Kimi Antonelli, Campione del mondo di Formula 1 Antonelli spoke with the highest office of the Italian state, explaining to him the sensations of wearing a helmet during a race, but also what driving a Formula 1 single-seater entails from a physical point of view. "You lose roughly a couple of kilograms," he said. "We have the fireproof suit, which is also hot. We train to be as ready as we can and to be able to withstand the heat we experience when we drive. But then after the session you jump into a tub of cold water..." The president then asked: "But was it like that in Formula 2 as well? And in karts?" "In karts a little less so," Antonelli replied. "You are much more out in the open. In a single-seater you are enclosed. But in F2 the races last a little less and are less physical. In Formula 1 the race lasts an average of an hour and a half. But will you come and see some races next year? Maybe at Monza? It would be very nice to have you with us." Il casco donato da Andrea Kimi Antonelli al Presidente della Repubblica, Sergio Mattarella Il casco donato da Andrea Kimi Antonelli al Presidente della Repubblica, Sergio Mattarella Mattarella, with a smile, replied: "I really hope so. Now Formula 1 attracts me a lot! The last time was several years ago. It is always complicated, because my movements are complex... But this new situation [referring to Antonelli's competitiveness] greatly encourages me." The meeting with the president was only the latest of Antonelli's engagements. A few hours earlier, Antonelli had attended the match between the Italian men's national football team and the French side, which Italy won 3-1, while the previous day he had stopped in San Marino - where he currently lives - to celebrate the world title. Antonelli will fly back to the United States, this time to Nevada, to contest the third-to-last round of the 2026 Formula 1 season in Las Vegas. top.title: Jurgen Klopp urges Germany to embrace "exceptional" quality after Nations League victory over Serbia
top.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-SRB-GER - AFP Jurgen Klopp has urged his Germany side to embrace their growing status as a European powerhouse following a dominant 3-1 victory over Serbia in the Nations League. The former Liverpool boss was full of praise for his team's tactical discipline and intensity as they moved a step closer to the quarter-finals. Klopp reflects on dominant display Germany took a significant step toward the Nations League quarter-finals on Thursday night, comfortably dispatching Serbia 3:1 on the road . Reflecting on the dominant display, Klopp insisted that his players must start recognising their own potential as they continue to evolve under his leadership. The result leaves Germany in a strong position in their group, shifting the focus to a high-stakes final fixture in Berlin. "The team played a really, really great game," Klopp told Sky Germany . "I think we have to get used to the fact that we are really good, that we can be really good. To be able to appreciate that correctly: of course we could score more goals today. But I just told the boys: 'I don't really care about that for the moment.' Because we can't say: 'We are starting processes and a development' - and then expect every time we look briefly: 'We must already be further ahead.' Even for ourselves, not just on the outside, for ourselves." Praises total control in hostile Serbia Klopp heaped praise on his side for navigating a hostile away environment unscathed, highlighting their composure as tensions boiled over. Despite facing a struggling Serbia outfit in a notoriously tricky fixture, the German tactician was delighted that his squad avoided any costly injury setbacks while dictating the tempo from start to finish. "It was outstandingly good in so many moments today, so difficult for Serbia, who are certainly not in their best moment. And yet you can really hurt yourself in such games - we didn't at all. So many sequences looked wonderful. In possession we had solutions, were dominant. The counter-pressing was outstanding. Intensity top. So, from my side, a really, really good game," the strategist added. top.title: “Are You Gonna Die?” – Alexander Zverev’s Unexpected Comment Toward Journalist Draws Priceless Reaction From Ben Shelton At ATP Finals
top.description: Alexander Zverev © Imagn images Alexander Zverev shared a hilarious moment with Ben Shelton and a reporter during the ATP Finals pre-tournament press conference. Zverev, Ben Shelton, Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar attended the press conference and a group photo on Friday evening. One journalist told Zverev that he had met all 30 World No. 1 players and that the German player was the last on his list. “I’ve met all 30 No. 1s in the world, and you’re the last one; you’re welcome,” the journalist said. Zverev instinctively responded with a joke, asking: “I’m the last one. Are you gonna die?” Zverev’s response left Shelton in splits; the American was seen hiding his face with his hand and giggling. The ATP Finals will be held from Nov. 15-22. Zverev will face debutant Jodar on the opening day of action at the Inalpi Arena in the afternoon session, followed by a Shelton–Fils clash in the evening. Alexander Zverev on being called the ATP Finals favorite Alexander Zverev and Carlos Alcaraz are the top two seeds at the ATP Finals in Turin. During the pre-tournament press conference for the John McEnroe Group, Zverev shared his view on being referred to as the tournament favorite, saying it is unfair. Zverev added that he is focusing on the challenge posed by Ben Shelton, Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar. “I think we shouldn’t disrespect anybody,” Zverev said. “I don’t think about Carlos right now. I think about these three young gentlemen because we have a very strong group and everybody shows that they know how to play tennis, otherwise they would not be here. top.title: Real Madrid quartet stand out as Jose Mourinho’s most consistent players this season
top.description: Real Madrid quartet stand out as Jose Mourinho’s most consistent players this season Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham, Marc Cucurella and Yan Diomande have emerged as the only four Real Madrid players to feature in every competitive match before the November international break, making them crucial to Jose Mourinho’s plans. The quartet have all appeared in Real Madrid’s 12 La Liga fixtures and four Champions League matches, but their minutes reveal a clear difference between regular involvement and workload. On that note, the likes of Mbappe and Bellingham have carried the heaviest responsibilities, while Cucurella and Diomande have contributed through a combination of starts and substitute appearances. Mbappe and Bellingham carry the heaviest workload Mbappe leads the group with 1,428 minutes and is the only one to have started all 16 matches. He has completed 12 of those 16 games, which shows just how central the French forward has become to Mourinho’s attacking plans. Bellingham, who is in sensational form this season , follows with 1,305 minutes and 15 starts, having also featured as a substitute on the one occasion he was not named in the starting line-up against Elche. Bellingham has started all but one game for Real Madrid this season. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Cucurella has accumulated 1,104 minutes through 11 starts and five appearances from the bench. Diomande, meanwhile, has played 891 minutes, starting nine matches and entering as a substitute in the other seven. Diomande makes an impact despite fewer minutes Diomande’s contribution in Europe is particularly notable, as he has recorded two assists and one goal in just 177 Champions League minutes, including a goal in Madrid’s 4-1 victory over Leipzig at the Bernabeu. In fact, during Vinicius’ absence, the former RB Leipzig star performed admirably, forcing Mourinho into a serious rethink once the Brazilian returns to La Liga action after the international break. Similarly, Cucurella’s involvement has also varied considerably. The defender played the entire Madrid derby against Atletico but was introduced only in the 89th minute against Rayo Vallecano. Cucurella’s time has been distributed as a starter and as a substitute. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) He has appeared in all four Champions League matches and provided an assist in the away fixture against AEK Athens. His minutes point to a player whose role can change according to the demands of individual matches. Courtois and Valverde narrowly miss the record Meanwhile, Thibaut Courtois and Federico Valverde are the two players closest to matching the quartet’s appearance record. Courtois has played 1,350 minutes across 15 matches, while Valverde has accumulated 1,181 minutes in the same number of appearances. Interestingly, both have spent more time on the pitch than Cucurella and Diomande, despite missing one of Madrid’s 16 fixtures.

top.title: Olivia Miles reflects on ‘special’ Year 1 with Minnesota Lynx in a heartwarming admission
top.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Olivia Miles has penned a message following an impressive debut season in the WNBA with the Minnesota Lynx. Miles was one of the top performers in the league and has cemented herself as one of the best rookies in history. She managed 790 points in 2026, which is a new rookie-season record, surpassing the previous total of 769 that was set by Indiana Fever ace Caitlin Clark in 2024. Miles also managed 239 assists for the Lynx in the most recent campaign. She failed to surpass record holder Clark in that area (337) but she still managed to secure the second-most assists of any rookie ever in the WNBA. She wrote: “Finally had the time to realise what the f*** happened this year… “So grateful for the mems, the belief, the love. My circle continues to fuel me and Minnesota welcomed me with such open arms. “I learned a ton – to appreciate the triumphs and failures wholeheartedly. They provide meaning in all of this. But more importantly, to have unwavering faith in my vision. What a special way to spend year 1… can’t wait for the bee hive.” Miles’ Lynx finished first in the WNBA regular season but they failed to make the Finals on this occasion. They lost 2-0 to the New York Liberty in the first round of the playoffs, with Miles scoring 16 points across both games. top.title: Lakers Make Brutal Kevon Looney Assessment Amid 11-2 Start
top.description: Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers overhauled their roster in the summer, and center Kevon Looney was one of the many new faces they brought in. Looney was set to be the backup to fellow new arrival Walker Kessler , but the Lakers have quickly realized he isn’t up to the task, according to The Athletic’s Dan Woike . “This team really can’t afford to lose Kessler for any extended amount of time,” Woike said. “The Lakers have already decided that Kevon Looney isn’t a workable backup center, and they have limited trade assets to address that (at a time when supply for backup centers is low and demand around the league outside of the Lakers is high).” The Lakers gave up two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps to the Utah Jazz for Kessler and don’t have much draft capital left now. They can offer a 2032 first-round pick swap and three second-round picks in trades, and that might not be enough to get a quality backup big in this current market. The Lakers just have to hope that the Kessler, who has had a fine start to the season, stays upright. Now, all of the Lakers’ new arrivals haven’t hit the ground running the way he has, but Looney is the only one whose acquisition looks like a clear mistake at this point. The only positive you can point to is that the 30-year-old was given only a one-year, $3.9 million deal . Looney played in each of the Lakers’ first four games, and it appears head coach JJ Redick saw enough in them to take him out of the rotation entirely. The three-time NBA champion has featured in only two of their last nine games and didn’t even play a combined five minutes in them. The Lakers have resorted to playing Jarred Vanderbilt and new arrival Sandro Mamukelashvili at center when Kessler sits. top.title: Taylor-Brown wins in Dubai to top T100 standings
top.description: Georgia Taylor-Brown has finished on the podium in all three of her T100 races this season, finishing first in Dubai and Pamplona and third in Vancouver [Getty Images] British triathlete Georgia Taylor-Brown held on to win the penultimate race of the women's T100 season in Dubai and move top of the overall standings. The 2020 Olympic silver medallist claimed her second victory of the season in the fourth event of the campaign, with December's grand final in Qatar remaining. Taylor-Brown will take a six-point advantage over Switzerland's Julie Derron into that final event. The 32-year-old Mancunian, who is a former world champion in the shorter Olympic distance and finished third in this season's World Triathlon Series , is aiming for her first T100 world title. Taylor-Brown won her first T100 race - which includes a 2km swim, 80km bike ride and 18km run - in Spain in May and was third in Vancouver, Canada in August. She hit the front in Dubai just under 4km into the run and opened a 30-second advantage before holding off New Zealand's Nicole van der Kaay to win by just 10 seconds, finishing in three hours 35 minutes and 19 seconds. Derron, who took the lead in the overall standings with victory in Vancouver, was third in Dubai, finishing two minutes seven seconds behind Taylor-Brown. Britain's Kate Waugh, the 2025 champion, was ninth, just ahead of team-mate Lizzie Rayner. Waugh missed the opening two events of the season with a calf injury and is eighth overall heading into next month's Grand Final in Doha.

nigeria.description: As Nigeria joins the rest of the world to commemorate World Diabetes Day(WDD), marked annually on Nov. 14, health experts have warned that changing lifestyles and late detection are fuelling a diabetes crisis in the country. WDD is commemorated to raise awareness on prevention, early detection and care. Diabetes Mellitus, a chronic metabolic condition characterised by elevated blood sugar due to inability of the pancreas to produce enough insulin or impaired insulin action, has become a major public health concern, with complications including blindness, kidney failure, heart failure, stroke and limb amputation. According to the International Diabetes Federation (IDF) Diabetes Atlas, globally no fewer than 589 million adults live with diabetes, with 24.6 million in Africa. About 11 million adults live with the condition in Nigeria, with many unaware of their status. Experts said the disease, which could remain undetected for years without symptoms, was now killing more Nigerians than malaria, HIV and tuberculosis combined. An Endocrinologist, Prof. Michael Olamoyegun, said diabetes killed more Nigerians than malaria, HIV and tuberculosis combined. Olamoyegun is Professor of Medicine and Endocrinology at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology and also Consultant Physician and Endocrinologist at LAUTECH Teaching Hospital, Ogbomoso, Oyo State. He said diabetes is a metabolic disorder of carbohydrates, fats and protein. He added that it is characterised by elevated blood sugar due to inability of pancreas to produce enough insulin. According to him, diabetes also occurs if insulin action is impaired. He said there are many variants but three main types existed – Type 1, Type 2 and Gestational Diabetes. ” Type 1 diabetes, which occurs due to absolute deficiency of insulin, is seen mainly in younger age group, usually less than 30 years, although occasionally in adulthood. “It is found in about five to ten per cent of all individuals with diabetes. “This group is managed with insulin injections since the body no longer produces insulin.” The endocrinologist said Type 2 diabetes represented 90 to 95 per cent of individuals with diabetes, stressing it occurred when insulin was not able to function well in the body. He also noted that it usually occurred in older individuals who had family history in first-degree relatives. Olamoyegun, also the Secretary General of the Association of Clinical Endocrinologists of Nigeria (ACEN), added that hypertension, overweight or obesity and sedentary lifestyles were contributory risk factors. nigeria.title: Airspace Now ‘Opened Up,’ No Cyberattack — US
nigeria.description: The United States on Friday lifted an hours-long ground stop at the nation’s airports, with top officials explaining that the disruption was due to old equipment and not a cyberattack or sweeping Microsoft outage. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told a late-night briefing at the White House that US airspace was now “opened up,” while warning it would take time for the travel chaos to clear. “At 8:15 tonight Eastern Time, we’ve opened up the airspace,” Duffy said. “Now does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It’s going to be slow.” Passengers wait for updates at a check-in area at Terminal 7 at Los Angeles International Airport, in Los Angeles on November 13, 2026. US aviation regulators issued an extremely rare ground stop of all flights across the country on November 13 after a major communications outage which the Department of Homeland Security said did not appear to be the result of any “nefarious attack.” The breakdown came a day after Duffy and the White House had formally asked Congress for $30 billion to upgrade and modernize the US Air Traffic Control System. “Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data, and they went down,” Duffy said. “It’s the old hardware that went down, and I think the question for the American people is: Do you want your Congress to fund this?” Duffy, however, insisted it was still safe for Americans to fly. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin dismissed speculation about a coordinated cyber assault on the United States, or any link to the Microsoft outage that affected services worldwide. “Welcome to Friday the 13th, right? You know, I want to make sure everybody understands that there is no connection between this and Microsoft. I know a lot of people are making that jump,” Mullin said. Mullin added there was “actually no cyber attack.” “When we start looking at cyber threats, cyber attacks, typically some people are going to raise their hand up and say, ‘Hey, we did that.’ There’s no chatter.’ We haven’t seen any footprints,” he added. But he said US security and law enforcement agencies were still checking and had ruled nothing out. Passengers wait in line to retrieve their luggage as flights were cancelled at Chicago O’Hare International Airport in Chicago on November 13, 2026. The two officials also defended President Donald Trump, who had yet to comment on the air stoppage some five hours after it began. “President Trump immediately had people in his office,” Mullin said. “We were communicating.” Passengers wait at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, Washington, DC on November 13, 2026. The players received national honours, three-bedroom apartments in Abuja and the promise of the naira equivalent of $100,000 each. The financial rewards were eventually fulfilled in November 2026. They trained hard, carried the green-and-white flag with pride and earned their moment in the sun. Their achievement deserves recognition, and the decision to preserve their rewards in savings instruments rather than hand enormous sums directly to teenagers is commendable. nigeria.description: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said Friday. Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said. The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters. “The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. One of the major conflicts dominating Trump’s second term as president will feature, but the other will not, the US officials said. “I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin,” a senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call. Washington has a “whole other track” of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, the official added, referring to talks that US envoys have had in recent days with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. “China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn’t seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there,” the official added. Tesla and Space X boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but won’t be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said. Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Thursday — their fourth meeting since the US president’s return to power last year. But Trump is not scheduled to have a separate one-on-one with Putin. Among other topics, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s resignation over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is not expected to come up in Trump’s meetings with Xi, the officials said. “The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip,” a second US senior official said. Trump will leave Washington on Monday and arrive in the Philippines on Tuesday for a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit before heading to Shenzhen. nigeria.description: Lethal autonomous weapons powered by artificial intelligence are set to revolutionise warfare but there is no proper regulatory or legal framework governing the new technology. Read Also: 6,000 Flight Cancelled: US air travel resumption will ‘take time’ A conference starting Monday at the United Nations in Geneva will discuss how to establish curbs and prohibitions on such weapons, called killer robots by some. But some analysts doubt the discussions at the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) will keep pace with the fast-changing weapons. AFP looks at three key questions ahead of the conference. What are LAWS? Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS) “can identify, select, and engage a target without the intervention of a human operator in the execution of these tasks,” said Jean-Marc Rickli, head of global and emerging risks at the Geneva Centre for Security Policy. Autonomous weapons have long existed. An anti-personnel mine “is an autonomous weapon in the sense that it explodes when someone steps on it,” said Laure de Roucy-Rochegonde of the Centre for Geopolitics of Technology at the French Institute of International Relations (IFRI). But with the proliferation of AI-enhanced drones, such weapons are now “capable of selecting and engaging a target that was not predetermined, adapting to their environment without human intervention,” said Rickli. So the critical issue for potential regulators lies in determining the level of human control over the decision to employ such a weapon. The United States refers to an “appropriate levels of human judgement” in the use of autonomous weapons. France maintains that a human must remain in the decision-making loop and bans “lethal autonomous weapons systems” (LAWS) but permits “partially autonomous” systems known as PLAWS. “The human role is always ensured through what is termed ‘appropriate control’ by a military commander — a concept that varies in scope depending on the system’s criticality and the operational context,” said Rear Admiral Vincent Sebastien, deputy director of the French defence ministry’s Agency for Defence Artificial Intelligence (AMIAD). The ethical issues? “We are now dangerously close to crossing a moral red line: the autonomous targeting of humans by machines,” UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, and International Committee of the Red Cross president Mirjana Spoljaric warned in a joint statement in August. But analysts said the Geneva discussions, while important, will touch only part of the issue. Today, the diminishing role of humans is being driven by the growing use of AI in analysis and targeting. What are you offering people now to make sure that tomorrow they believe?” he asked. “People today need to be very, very confident. entertainment.description: The Forum for Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) successfully concluded its 2026 annual convention on Thursday, October 29, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos, Nigeria. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. The challenge was that the new management structure had not been properly implemented within the organisation. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. The wobbly Nigerian economy doesn’t help matters either, as people are putting off marriage till they can grow their finances, leading to advanced marital age across both genders. For instance, I have several male ex-classmates in their 40s who have given up on getting married because they cannot afford to. This is very unfortunate. entertainment.title: Toni Tones and Jim Iyke Are Bringing Drama to KAVA This November — See the Official Poster
entertainment.description: The Nigerian thriller series, directed by Wande Thomas and produced by Isoken Ogiemwonyi, is set to join KAVA’s growing slate of premium African content. Nigerian streaming platform KAVA is set to bring the psychological thriller series Spiraling , starring Toni Tones ( King of Boys ) and Jim Iyke , to audiences across its streaming service. Set against the high-stakes worlds of technology, power and politics in contemporary Nigeria, Spiraling follows Sade ( Toni Tones ), a brilliant tech entrepreneur whose carefully constructed life begins to unravel after an impulsive affair triggers a dangerous chain of events. Spiraling explores the darker side of ambition and the lengths people will go to protect their carefully constructed lives. Alongside Tones and Iyke, the ensemble cast includes Folu Storms , Seun Ajayi , Fae Olumide , Fiyinfoluwa Asenuga and Mathilda Akatugba . Created and directed by Wande Thomas ( Under the Influence , The Smart Money Woman ), the series is co-written by Thomas and Amaka Anioji and produced by Isoken Ogiemwonyi ( The Smart Money Woman , Ci ) . Director and creator Wande Thomas added: I wanted to explore how quickly an ordinary decision can spiral into something completely beyond your control. At its heart, this is a story about the secrets we keep, the lies we tell ourselves and how far we’ll go when everything is at stake. I’m excited for audiences to finally experience it. F Taofeeq/Spiraling Producer Isoken Ogiemwonyi said: With Spiraling , we wanted to take a simple story and tell it really well. We spent a lot of time developing the characters and exploring the darker side of very human emotions, ambition, desire and jealousy. At its heart, it’s a character-driven story about flawed people making questionable decisions, and we’re excited to partner with KAVA to bring it to audiences across Africa and the diaspora. Ladun Awobokun , Head of Acquisitions at KAVA commented : Spiraling is exactly the kind of bold, sophisticated African storytelling we want to champion at KAVA. With its compelling performances and distinctly Nigerian setting, the series delivers a gripping thriller that we believe will resonate with audiences at home and around the world. We’re delighted to bring it to our viewers. Spiraling will be available to stream on KAVA on the 26th of November. Follow @spiralingseries for updates. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. entertainment.title: Olamide’s Time & Space Is Almost Here! See the Cover Art & 10 Track List
entertainment.description: Olamide releases his new single Burukutu alongside his upcoming album Time & Space. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram If Olamide ‘s ‘ Burukutu ‘ has been on repeat, here’s something else to get into: the rapper has revealed the cover art and full tracklist for his upcoming album, Time & Space . Scheduled for release on November 16, 2026, under YBNL Nation and EMPIRE, the ten-track body of work follows a remarkable lineage of musical evolution from one of Africa’s most enduring creative forces. Adding a deeply personal touch to the rollout, Olamide revealed that he personally painted the striking cover art for the project. Olamide hand-painted the official artwork for his upcoming Time & Space, released via YBNL Nation and EMPIRE. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram Listeners have already caught an exciting glimpse of what to expect from the record through the release of the lead single, Burukutu . Named after the traditional, locally brewed fermented grain beverage, the track serves up rich street-level jubilation and celebratory culture, anchored by rhythmic cadences and unmistakable Yoruba-inflected delivery. The musical journey of Time & Space spans ten carefully curated titles designed to showcase his artistic range. The newly revealed tracklist opens with “ Elohim ” as the introductory piece, followed sequentially by “ Skoskola “, “ Say Less “, the lead anthem “ Burukutu “, and “ Alujon ” rounding out the first half. As November 16 approaches, anticipation continues to build across Lagos and beyond, cementing yet another brilliant chapter in Olamide’s legendary catalogue. entertainment.description: Alex Unusual’s gold grillz, crystal floral choker, and cherub-accented sunglasses. Who says a buba has to be paired with a wrapper? Nigerian actress, media personality, and reality television star Asogwa Alexandra A —popularly known as Alex Unusua l—is giving us another way to wear the traditional Yoruba top, and her look for the premiere of Loving Itohan makes a strong case for pairing it with a mini skirt. The actress chose a bright fuchsia satin buba with wide half-sleeves, styling it with a fitted mini skirt made from emerald-green and magenta floral brocade damask . It’s an interesting way to rethink the familiar iro and bubacombination: keep the traditional top, swap the wrapper for a shorter skirt, and let the difference in fabric and colour give the outfit its character. The smooth finish of the pink satin against the patterned damask also shows how to wear two statement fabrics without making them compete . The trick is to give each piece a clear role, with the pink buba providing a bold block of colour and the brocade bringing in pattern and texture. Alex Unusual puts a modern spin on the Yoruba iro and buba with a satin top and brocade mini skirt. The mini skirt also gives the outfit a contemporary take on the Oleku silhouette, which traditionally pairs a loose or fitted buba with a wrapper tied above the knee. Alex’s version plays with that familiar proportion, using a fitted damask skirt in place of the wrapper. If you are wondering how to wear a buba and mini skirt without the proportions feeling off, the secret is balancing volume with structure. Because a traditional buba comes with a relaxed cut and wide sleeves, tucking it cleanly into a fitted, high-waisted mini skirt defines the waist and keeps the silhouette neat rather than boxy. Mixing textures intentionally helps too—pairing a plain silk, satin, or AsoOke top with a patterned damask, jacquard, or beaded mini skirt lets both pieces complement each other rather than clash. Using the same fabric for the skirt and gele also helped bring the different parts of the outfit together, while keeping the pink buba at the centre of the colour story. sports.description: Jürgen Klopp praises Brajan Gruda after stunning goal on Germany debut An assist against Manchester City, two against FC Augsburg and now a goal on his debut for the Germany senior national team . Brajan Gruda was named in the starting XI for Germany’s 3-1 win over Serbia in the Nations League, wearing the number ten shirt. Head coach Jürgen Klopp had already described the Leipzig attacker as a “street footballer, simply a brilliant player to watch” ahead of the match. Gruda with a solo run from his own half Operating on the right wing, Brajan repeatedly looked to take on his man against a Serbia side sitting deep. After around 20 minutes, he delivered a pinpoint cross onto the head of Kai Havertz. Shortly after the break, Gruda embarked on a solo run during a spell of Serbian pressure. Receiving a low pass from Joshua Kimmich, he turned away from his marker inside his own half . Approaching the penalty area, he left another defender trailing before slotting a low left-footed finish into the bottom-right corner . Nine successful dribbles on Germany debut - only Jamal Musiala has managed more Against Serbia, Brajan completed nine of his 14 attempted dribbles . According to Opta, only Jamal Musiala has recorded more successful dribbles in a single appearance for Germany over the past ten years. Musiala managed 13 against Costa Rica at the 2022 World Cup. “ It was instinct. I don’t think too much when I’m dribbling with the ball. I just do it . It just happens,” Brajan said of his goal. Klopp summed up the moment in his interview with RTL: “Brajan then calmly put an end to the opposition’s brief resurgence.” Klopp raves about Gruda’s feel for the game “What a debut,” said RTL commentator Wolff-Christoph Fuss as Brajan was substituted off in the 86th minute. Klopp was particularly impressed by the way Gruda switched between keeping things simple and taking on opponents with daring dribbles. “Brajan is an exceptional talent ; he has exceptional ability . The way he mixed things up today, playing simple passes before taking risks again – it was really lovely to watch .” Germany face the Netherlands on Monday evening. sports.title: Kimi Antonelli meets Italian president Sergio Mattarella
sports.description: Motorsport photo "To President Mattarella, with great admiration," signed Kimi Antonelli . The new Formula 1 world champion is in the middle of a whirlwind of meetings, events and celebrations for the world title he won two weeks ago at the Mexico Grand Prix, with which he ended a title drought for an Italian driver to win the world championship dating back to 1953. Antonelli, together with his parents Marco and Veronica and his sister Maggie, was received on Friday by the president of the Italian Republic, Sergio Mattarella. The meeting took place at the Quirinale in Rome, with Antonelli giving the president one of his official helmets with a dedication written on the visor. Il Presidente Sergio Mattarella con Kimi Antonelli, Campione del mondo di Formula 1 Il Presidente Sergio Mattarella con Kimi Antonelli, Campione del mondo di Formula 1 Antonelli spoke with the highest office of the Italian state, explaining to him the sensations of wearing a helmet during a race, but also what driving a Formula 1 single-seater entails from a physical point of view. "You lose roughly a couple of kilograms," he said. "We have the fireproof suit, which is also hot. We train to be as ready as we can and to be able to withstand the heat we experience when we drive. But then after the session you jump into a tub of cold water..." The president then asked: "But was it like that in Formula 2 as well? And in karts?" "In karts a little less so," Antonelli replied. "You are much more out in the open. In a single-seater you are enclosed. But in F2 the races last a little less and are less physical. In Formula 1 the race lasts an average of an hour and a half. But will you come and see some races next year? Maybe at Monza? It would be very nice to have you with us." Now Formula 1 attracts me a lot! The last time was several years ago. It is always complicated, because my movements are complex... But this new situation [referring to Antonelli's competitiveness] greatly encourages me." The meeting with the president was only the latest of Antonelli's engagements. A few hours earlier, Antonelli had attended the match between the Italian men's national football team and the French side, which Italy won 3-1, while the previous day he had stopped in San Marino - where he currently lives - to celebrate the world title. sports.description: Real Madrid quartet stand out as Jose Mourinho’s most consistent players this season Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham, Marc Cucurella and Yan Diomande have emerged as the only four Real Madrid players to feature in every competitive match before the November international break, making them crucial to Jose Mourinho’s plans. The quartet have all appeared in Real Madrid’s 12 La Liga fixtures and four Champions League matches, but their minutes reveal a clear difference between regular involvement and workload. On that note, the likes of Mbappe and Bellingham have carried the heaviest responsibilities, while Cucurella and Diomande have contributed through a combination of starts and substitute appearances. Mbappe and Bellingham carry the heaviest workload Mbappe leads the group with 1,428 minutes and is the only one to have started all 16 matches. He has completed 12 of those 16 games, which shows just how central the French forward has become to Mourinho’s attacking plans. Bellingham, who is in sensational form this season , follows with 1,305 minutes and 15 starts, having also featured as a substitute on the one occasion he was not named in the starting line-up against Elche. Bellingham has started all but one game for Real Madrid this season. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Cucurella has accumulated 1,104 minutes through 11 starts and five appearances from the bench. Diomande, meanwhile, has played 891 minutes, starting nine matches and entering as a substitute in the other seven. Diomande makes an impact despite fewer minutes Diomande’s contribution in Europe is particularly notable, as he has recorded two assists and one goal in just 177 Champions League minutes, including a goal in Madrid’s 4-1 victory over Leipzig at the Bernabeu. In fact, during Vinicius’ absence, the former RB Leipzig star performed admirably, forcing Mourinho into a serious rethink once the Brazilian returns to La Liga action after the international break. Similarly, Cucurella’s involvement has also varied considerably. The defender played the entire Madrid derby against Atletico but was introduced only in the 89th minute against Rayo Vallecano. Cucurella’s time has been distributed as a starter and as a substitute. Courtois has played 1,350 minutes across 15 matches, while Valverde has accumulated 1,181 minutes in the same number of appearances. Interestingly, both have spent more time on the pitch than Cucurella and Diomande, despite missing one of Madrid’s 16 fixtures.

sports.description: Georgia Taylor-Brown has finished on the podium in all three of her T100 races this season, finishing first in Dubai and Pamplona and third in Vancouver [Getty Images] British triathlete Georgia Taylor-Brown held on to win the penultimate race of the women's T100 season in Dubai and move top of the overall standings. The 2020 Olympic silver medallist claimed her second victory of the season in the fourth event of the campaign, with December's grand final in Qatar remaining. Taylor-Brown will take a six-point advantage over Switzerland's Julie Derron into that final event. The 32-year-old Mancunian, who is a former world champion in the shorter Olympic distance and finished third in this season's World Triathlon Series , is aiming for her first T100 world title. Taylor-Brown won her first T100 race - which includes a 2km swim, 80km bike ride and 18km run - in Spain in May and was third in Vancouver, Canada in August. She hit the front in Dubai just under 4km into the run and opened a 30-second advantage before holding off New Zealand's Nicole van der Kaay to win by just 10 seconds, finishing in three hours 35 minutes and 19 seconds. Derron, who took the lead in the overall standings with victory in Vancouver, was third in Dubai, finishing two minutes seven seconds behind Taylor-Brown. Britain's Kate Waugh, the 2025 champion, was ninth, just ahead of team-mate Lizzie Rayner. Waugh missed the opening two events of the season with a calf injury and is eighth overall heading into next month's Grand Final in Doha.

sports.title: Verstappen faster than everyone: promising figures for Las Vegas
sports.description: Max Verstappen heads to Las Vegas with a second-place finish in Brazil under his belt, where low temperatures are once again expected. An analysis of race pace at Interlagos shows that Red Bull Racing was able to match McLaren and Mercedes in a range of conditions. One particular statistic from the dry phase offers hope for the Dutchman. Verstappen started the Brazilian Grand Prix from 21st on the grid and fought his way up to second place in changeable conditions. Teammate Isack Hadjar finished third, giving Red Bull its second double podium of the year. Conditions played an important role in the result. The race began on a wet track, after which the drivers switched to slicks. Rain returned in the closing stages. These different phases make it possible to compare Red Bull’s performance in wet and dry conditions. The pace on the soft tyres is particularly interesting ahead of Las Vegas, where qualifying and the race are expected to take place in temperatures of around ten degrees. Verstappen faster than McLaren on slicks in Brazil The gaps between Red Bull, McLaren and Mercedes were particularly small during the wet phases. The five fastest drivers on intermediates were separated by just over a tenth of a second. Norris recorded the lowest median lap time, but Hadjar and Verstappen were close behind. Hadjar, in particular, showed that he was comfortable in the changing conditions. Over the entire race on intermediates, the French-Algerian driver was slightly faster than Verstappen and even recorded the best median lap time among the drivers studied during the final spell of rain. The picture changed as the track dried out. Verstappen was the fastest of the eight drivers studied on the soft tyre, with a narrow advantage over Norris and Oscar Piastri. Antonelli was also a few tenths off the pace. Hadjar dropped to fifth in this comparison, more than three tenths behind his teammate. The gaps are small, but they suggest that Verstappen’s performance during the dry phase was not solely down to his charge through the field in the rain. He also had enough pace on slicks to take the fight to the McLarens. One caveat is that tyre age and any delays or difficulties caused by traffic are not factored into the averages, as that data is unavailable. No signs of a major Red Bull disadvantage in tyre degradation The progression of the dry stints also offers some interesting insights. Verstappen completed his first 28 laps on the soft tyre before receiving a fresh set. His median lap time in the second stint was around 1.7 seconds lower. Hadjar gained almost a second and a half on new rubber, while Norris and Piastri also became significantly faster. These improvements cannot be attributed solely to tyre wear. The cars were lighter later in the race, and track conditions changed as well. It is, however, worth noting that these figures do not suggest an exceptionally large drop-off for Red Bull compared with McLaren. This is relevant to Verstappen’s prospects.

technology.title: Microsoft's school email bill gives rivals something to smile about
technology.description: The fallout from Microsoft's education price rises and service cuts continues as institutions weigh the prospect of bigger bills, and the Windows maker's rivals struggle not to pull "I told you so" faces. The main takeaways are that free student email and collaboration services are being retired, and storage entitlements are changing. These changes generally apply at institutions' first renewal or extension on or after January 1, 2028. Microsoft announced the new plans last week, and the UK's Department for Education described itself as "disappointed" at the news. As well it might be, although the UK government has rarely seen a deal from Microsoft that it didn't like . Or, for that matter, other US tech giants . Exactly how much educational institutions will have to spend remains unclear. Mary Jo Foley of Directions on Microsoft put indicative student pricing at $2 per year for Microsoft 365 Education A2, $4 for A3, and $6 for A5, with Teams adding another dollar annually. Faculty licenses cost considerably more, while the new A7 student tier jumps to $385 a year before Teams. Foley cautioned that these were approximate figures, with actual prices set by Microsoft's partners. The new no-cost student tier, Microsoft 365 Education A0, is a poor replacement for Office 365 A1: it excludes Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and Teams. Eligibility also requires full paid faculty coverage on A2 or higher and students who actively use Windows devices for education – potentially awkward for institutions running fleets of Chromebooks. A few dollars per student might not sound alarming. Multiply that across an institution, however, and something that used to be free becomes a recurring bill. Michael Meeks, CEO of Collabora Productivity, told The Register: "Free was the bait on the hook, and Microsoft spent years reeling in schools' email accounts, documents, identity management and classrooms onto its cloud." A poster on the edugeek.net forums commented: "This was always going to happen, I remember thinking this when we moved over to the MS free cloud solution. It will be free until they decide it isn't." The risk for Microsoft is that there are options. Meeks told us: "Schools now have a year to plan, and, in our experience with other large-scale educational projects, such as the University of Lille, that can be enough time to migrate properly." Other options include Nextcloud, which will be rolled out as part of Germany's Educational Cloud Infrastructure . Several Swiss universities also migrated to the service over an August weekend. According to Nextcloud, 39,500 students, teachers, and researchers, along with 585 terabytes of data, were shifted. technology.title: Big Tech takes a beating as online safety experts accuse companies of doing bare minimum
technology.description: Technology companies are doing just enough to show a degree of compliance with the UK's Online Safety Act, but are failing to meet the needs of the individuals and young victims the legislation exists to protect, experts say. A panel of online safety pros assembled before Parliament's Communications and Digital Committee on Tuesday, taking aim at the likes of Google, Microsoft, Meta, and ByteDance for failing to act on important matters. Clare McGlynn, professor of law at Durham University and expert on violence against women and girls (VAWG), was especially critical of major search engine providers for their inconsistent downranking of harmful content search terms. "Rape porn," for example, is correctly downranked and no user sees any relevant links until the tenth page of results, although adjacent terms such as "unwilling porn" can be found as early as the third page, McGlynn said. "I just think if someone spent a little more time thinking 'I really want to minimize the risk of this material appearing,' I would take a systematic approach," she told the committee. "I would downrank 'unwilling' and 'unwanted,' and I would downrank 'asleep porn' as well… because it just means that it's easily findable. "So, they don't rank some of them, but just not systematically or wholly consistently." McGlynn went on to say that during her own research, "force porn" was rightly downranked heavily, although terms as similar as "forced porn" were not. "If you were trying to think of the words that would be similar to say rape, and rape porn is extreme porn and it's not supposed to be on those platforms anymore, you would think of words like unwilling and unwanted," she added. "And we know your algorithm would." Google inevitably took much of McGlynn's flak due to its dominance of the search engine market, although the professor said the same issues can be observed on Bing, too. Alexandra Whiston-Dew, partner at law firm Miscon de Raya, argued that search engines have such an important role in regulating the OSA, noting the limited resources at Ofcom's disposal. She said that more needs to be done from the tech side to ensure different parties in the chain of publication are detected early and downranked or blocked accordingly. There are publications, for example, that actively advertise themselves as websites that host illegal content, and these appear to be missing from the search engines' crosshairs. "So, they are spotlighting the fact that they are publishing illegal content, and this is going under the radar not only from the search engines but also the other platforms and the businesses in the chain of publication," said Whiston-Dew. "Also Ofcom needs to really pull all of their resources together and attack that receptacle of illegal content." technology.title: Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed
technology.description: GLP-1 medications are everywhere these days. The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. But, amid the boom, the latest data suggests millions of Americans have turned to unapproved versions and are using the potent drugs in ways doctors never intended, raising questions about what that real-world use means for safety and efficacy. In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That's around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. Among GLP-1 users, nearly half (44 percent) reported using their GLP-1 in a way that was different from how it was prescribed. Users skipped doses, delayed getting refills, and used smaller doses than prescribed, among other changes. More than half of the people modifying how they used the drug said the changes were because of cost or availability reasons. Cost and access barriers were most pronounced among younger GLP-1 users. technology.description: Chalk up a new record for vulns. The number of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) found and disclosed so far in 2026 surpassed 100,000 on Friday - more than double 2025’s total - and the reason can be summed up in two letters: AI. “It’s kind of wild,” Josh Bressers, VulnCheck’s director of coordinated vulnerability disclosure, told The Register . “The thing that almost scares the bejesus out of me is while 100K sounds like a lot, in a couple years we're going to say, remember when it was only 100K?” As of the time of our interview, about 4 pm UTC on Friday, VulnCheck counted 100,222 CVEs, he said. Microsoft alone added 1,094 security flaws to the total count on Tuesday, following 1,474 vulnerabilities the month before. “There's no denying the fact that vulnerability hunting with AI is driving a majority of what we're seeing.” All the major CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs) - these are the organizations authorized by the CVE program to assign unique identifiers to security vulnerabilities - like VulnCheck, Microsoft, Oracle, GitHub, and other large enterprise IT vendors “are just screaming into the atmosphere right now,” Bressers said. “It’s AI.” Meanwhile, the percentage of these bugs that are exploited in the wild remains relatively consistent. About 1.4 percent (1,363) of the CVEs published this year have been added to VulnCheck’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. “But obviously, as the number of CVEs grows, [1 percent] of 1,000 is a lot different than [1 percent] of 100,000,” Bressers said. Plus, as other security researchers have documented, the window between the public release of a security patch and attackers developing working exploits – often by reverse engineering the patch while end users are still applying the fix – is rapidly shrinking. technology.description: The internet is full of schlock, from biased news and dubious hot takes to false factoids. LogicLens aims to separate fact from fiction using the very same technology behind some of that slop: AI. It’s a simple premise, really: LogicLens, which lives in Chrome as a browser extension , or on iOS in the form of a mobile app called Receipts , combs through articles, social media posts, and other content to check it not only for factual inaccuracies, but also for bad reasoning. LogicLens and Receipts claim to identify logical fallacies , flag reports that misrepresent information, detect content that attempts to polarize an issue, and the like. It also cites sources, so if, for example, you need to call someone out on their BS, you’ll have ammunition. Or, if you’re trying to fact-check something before sharing it, you can get a more accurate view of the situation, and maybe post something else instead. Using the Chrome extension is as simple as clicking on its icon in the list of extensions in the browser. On iOS, the Receipts app is found as a share option. Once it starts, LogicLens scans an article, post, video, etc. to find potential issues of factual or logical inconsistency and flags them for review. If the facts of the matter turn out to contradict your worldview, LogicLens’ creators say they’re not trying to be partisan - you may just not be as informed as you need to be, which hopefully their tool will assist with. “We're not trying to be the referee of truth,” the company’s about page states. “Instead, LogicLens helps uncover the context, so you can decide for yourself without the spin." Of course, AI is increasingly used for online analysis and content review, and LogicLens is no exception. technology.title: In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits
technology.description: Elephants live in some of the most complex and resilient societies in the animal kingdom. Individuals die or move away, calves grow up, and newcomers join, but the local communities as a whole usually hold together. Long-term studies of African savanna elephants have shown that, even after poaching or other spikes in deaths, survivors tend to rebuild their lost connections over time. But a new study suggests that resilience may not keep the community intact when steady losses accumulate over time. Anastasia Madsen, a behavioral ecologist at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues analyzed 12 years of observations of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka. They found that, once losses began to outpace newcomers, the elephants’ society didn’t just get smaller. It fractured. Accidental savanna Udawalawe National Park in southern Sri Lanka was created in the 1970s around a reservoir on one of the country's four major rivers. “Before that, it was basically a tropical deciduous forest,” said Shermin de Silva, an ecologist at UC San Diego and senior author of the study (de Silva started the Udawalawe Elephant Research Project in 2006). science.title: New Scientist readers on how the magazine has shaped their lives
science.description: Have you been reading New Scientist since the start? Getty Images/Westend61 The first issue of New Scientist was published on 22 November 1956, and some of our readers have been with us since the very beginning. We asked subscribers, young and old, to tell us how they first encountered the magazine and how New Scientist has influenced their lives. The volume of responses and the gratitude expressed within them were quite overwhelming. Here are some of our favourites, featuring a spectacular maggot experiment, science-inspired poetry and even a match made on the short-lived New Scientist dating site. Huge thanks to everyone who wrote in. I was interested to see that New Scientist was launched “for all those men and women who are interested in scientific discovery and in its industrial, commercial and social consequences”. At the age of 13, I saved up a shilling from my Saturday morning “jobs” to purchase the first edition on 22 November 1956 and became one of those people interested in scientific discovery. Seventy years later, I remain a subscriber, after a scientific career that took me to many (if not, most!) countries in the world. New Scientist covered things like the opening of Jodrell Bank telescope in 1957. Since that was only about 50 miles (80 kilometres) away, it necessitated a bike ride to see what it really looked like! Peter Hall Advertisement I seem to have been reading New Scientist for the full 70! I do recall my encounter with the first edition: I was at Bec Grammar School in south London in a second-year physics class – it was 1956. The teacher, a genial boffin-type, announced the advent of the new publication and handed out copies – all I remember is its grey (or was it beige?) pages, which I read in a perfunctory way (I was only 12!) little thinking it would follow me through life and around the globe. Robyn Williams I was at Malvern College in England for my O level examinations from 1955 to 1958. My science master at Malvern had recognised my interest in science and technology and he bought the very first issue of New Scientist with his own money. At the next science class, he stood up in front of the whole class and waved the first issue, saying, “Young Inman, a new UK science and technology magazine has been published and here is the first issue for you.” I went on to reach 60 years as a member of the UK Institution of Civil Engineers. Peter Inman 1956 puts me back at school – Fettes College in Edinburgh. The school adopted New Scientist from its first edition and it was available in the library, where senior boys interested in science were recommended to read it. And so began a lifetime of New Scientist – I have been a regular for as long as I can remember and a subscriber for a very long time. I am very grateful to New Scientist for maintaining my interest in all the sciences and new developments, which I am sure has helped me to think laterally and to have a greater understanding of what makes everything tick. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972. science.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
science.description: null This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed. In more recent years, most notably 1999 , 2001 and 2002 , lesser Leonid displays of up to "only" a few thousand meteors per hour took place. Unfortunately, that's not likely to be the case this year. In fact, comparatively speaking, this is going to be a lean year for the Leonids chiefly because of the expected lack of any significant activity. Although the Leonids are one of the most famous of all the annual meteor displays, this year they're not likely to be very productive. It's probable they are going to be rather weak and there probably will be long stretches when not a single Leonid will be seen. I'll explain why in a moment. First, let's find out about this shower's lineage. What causes the Leonids? The Leonids are so named because the shower's radiant point, from where the meteors seem to fan out, is located within the constellation of Leo the Lion, from the backward question mark pattern of stars known as " The Sickle." The meteors are caused by the Tempel-Tuttle comet , which sweeps through the inner solar system every 33⅓ years. Each time the comet passes closest to the sun it leaves a "river of rubble" in its wake: a dense trail of dusty debris. A meteor storm becomes possible if the Earth were to score a direct hit on a fresh dust trail ejected by the comet over the past several centuries. The "lion's share" (no pun intended) of comet dust can be found just ahead and trailing behind Tempel-Tuttle. That comet last swept through the inner solar system in 1998. That's why spectacular meteor showers were seen in 1999, 2001 and 2002, with declining numbers thereafter.
